summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type I diabetes, and severe coronary artery disease underwent a quadruple coronary artery bypass graft (CABG x4) for revascularization. Postoperatively, he remained intubated overnight and was extubated on postoperative day one. He experienced transient hyperglycemia requiring ICU readmission and insulin regimen adjustment with endocrinology consultation. A serosanguinous sternal wound drainage prompted a course of cephalexin, and a moderate left pleural effusion was noted but remained asymptomatic. He received hemodialysis throughout the admission and a single unit of packed red cells for anemia. He was successfully weaned from inotropic support, transferred to the floor, and cleared for discharge home on postoperative day seven with home health services. Discharge instructions emphasized wound care, activity restrictions, and close monitoring for signs of infection or fluid overload.
